ugli.e: A proprietary name, as an alteration of ugly, from the fruit's often lumpy and discolored appearance.

uglify.e: From ugly + -fy. Sense 3 by analogy with prettify.

s.d: make ugly
To make ugly; to destroy or worsen the appearance or attractiveness of.
x: She uglifies every thing near her.
These guys around that block had this thing about how I was uglifying the neighborhood.

s.d: To become ugly.
x: Inevitably those bodies age and uglify under her influence, but if they are outstandingly beautiful at the outset, that process takes longer.

s.d: Synonym of minify.

ugly.e:
Inherited from Middle English ugly, uggely, uglike, borrowed from Old Norse uggligr (“fearful, dreadful, horrible in appearance”), from uggr (“fear, apprehension, dread”) (possibly related to agg (“strife, hate”)), equivalent to ug + -ly. Cognate with Scots ugly, uglie, Icelandic ugglegur. Meaning softened to "very unpleasant to look at" around the late 14th century, and sense of "morally offensive" attested from around 1300.
